note: Roads, signposts and caravans of the open world (core/game/game_roads.gd, core/game/game_caravans.gd; drawn by ui/play/tile_view.gd and ui/play/roadside_art.gd; checked by tools/check_data.gd). Everything here is look and convenience: GameWorldGen's tile, height, water and node answer exactly as before. A tile is road when it lies within `half_width` tiles (plus or minus `wobble` of a hash of the tile, so the edge is ragged) of one of GameWorldGen.roads()'s straight links, on dry land, and not on the ground of a town, dungeon or plot. A road tile is drawn as a worn trail (one of 16 glyphs, `trail_<mask>`, by which of its four neighbours are road: ragged edges where the road ends, ruts and grit from `trail`) and a walker on it takes `pace` of the usual time between steps (1 off the road; below 1 is faster). Signposts stand beside the road: one `gap` tiles outside the ground of each place on each road that leaves it (`end`), one outside each town gate (`gate`), and one at each place two roads cross away from a place (`cross`), `side` tiles to one side of the road (the side is a hash), on the nearest free dry tile within `search`. A signpost names the places and how far each is (`tag_range` tiles from it the name tag shows over the post). Caravans: a wagon and its trader walk each road between two towns of `towns_only` at `tiles_per_hour` (a day is 24 hours, GameDay), wait `rest_hours` in each town, and set out at a time keyed on the seed and the road (`depart_hours` spreads them); pure of the seed, the road and the hour, nothing is saved but what the family buys (GameWildsTrade's marks). Use beside one (within `reach` tiles) opens the merchant panel with the wares of the landmark kind `caravan` (data/world/wilds.json). Nothing here draws a die of the dynasty's.
